1 Scope and artifact roles

This report consumes regenerated outputs under a new result root. The frozen Phase-0 report and artifacts are provisional/stale and are not used here. The primary result is whatever K the R AutoK run selected independently; it is never fixed to K=4 or K=11. The K=11 panel is a separate torch_gmm_fit() sensitivity fit corresponding to Cluster(n_clusters=11, random_state=12345). Its integer seed is matched, but R and Python use different initialization and random-number streams, so this does not claim seed-identical fitted parameters. Published H5AD cluster_cellcharter labels are retained only as a third reference artifact and are not plotted as the R tutorial fit.

role_table <- do.call(rbind, lapply(manifest$roles, function(x) data.frame(
  role_id = x$role_id,
  k = x$k,
  seed = if (is.na(x$seed)) "NA (not an R fit)" else as.character(x$seed),
  model_path = if (is.na(x$model_path)) "NA (published labels)" else x$model_path,
  cell_order_sha256 = x$cell_order_sha256,
  aggregation_data_id = x$aggregation_data_id,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)))
knitr::kable(role_table, caption = "Non-interchangeable analysis roles")

Only BALBc-1 and early MRL-4 are displayed in maps. Enrichment and proximity statistics use all nine libraries. The full cell_type annotation is used for the log2 observed/expected dot plot with size_threshold=0.58, color_threshold=0.58, and the CellCharter v0.2.0 default clustered labels.

2 From input SPE to saved results

The full mouse-spleen analysis is deliberately not rerun while this report is rendered. The code below shows the public stages used to create the graph, in-memory neighborhood representation, AutoK fit, selected domains, and downstream statistics. The evaluated sections that follow load the corresponding precomputed artifacts and display their outputs.

full_spe <- readRDS("results/CellCharterR_mouse_spleen_v2/representation/codex_sce.rds")

full_spe <- cellcharter_graph(
  full_spe,
  spatial = "spatial",
  sample_col = "sample",
  graph_name = "cellcharter_graph",
  percentile = 99
)

full_spe <- cellcharter_aggregate(
  full_spe,
  representation = "X_trVAE",
  graph_name = "cellcharter_graph",
  sample_col = "sample",
  output = "X_cellcharter",
  n_layers = 3L
)

saveRDS(
  full_spe,
  "results/CellCharterR_mouse_spleen_v2/aggregation/spe_after_aggregation.rds",
  compress = FALSE
)

full_spe <- cellcharter_cluster(
  full_spe,
  representation = "X_cellcharter",
  candidate_k = 2:20,
  checkpoint_dir = "results/CellCharterR_mouse_spleen_v2/autok",
  domain_col = "cellcharter_domain",
  max_runs = 10L,
  convergence_tol = 0.01,
  seed = 1L,
  fit_args = list(device = "auto", batch_size = 8192L),
  predict_args = list(device = "auto", batch_size = 8192L),
  resume = TRUE
)

full_spe <- cellcharter_enrichment(
  full_spe,
  group_col = "cell_type",
  domain_col = "cellcharter_domain"
)
full_spe <- cellcharter_nhood_enrichment(
  full_spe,
  graph_name = "cellcharter_graph",
  domain_col = "cellcharter_domain"
)
full_spe <- cellcharter_diff_nhood_enrichment(
  full_spe,
  graph_name = "cellcharter_graph",
  domain_col = "cellcharter_domain",
  condition_col = "condition",
  sample_col = "sample",
  condition_groups = c("BALBc", "MRL"),
  n_perms = 100L,
  seed = 1L
)

saveRDS(
  full_spe,
  "results/CellCharterR_mouse_spleen_v2/downstream/codex_spe_complete.rds"
)

2.1 Resume AutoK after an interruption

Keep the post-aggregation SPE and AutoK directory together. Days or weeks later, repeat the exact clustering call with resume = TRUE; completed run_*.rds fits are reused.

full_spe <- readRDS(
  "results/CellCharterR_mouse_spleen_v2/aggregation/spe_after_aggregation.rds"
)

full_spe <- cellcharter_cluster(
  full_spe,
  representation = "X_cellcharter",
  candidate_k = 2:20,
  checkpoint_dir = "results/CellCharterR_mouse_spleen_v2/autok",
  domain_col = "cellcharter_domain",
  max_runs = 10L,
  convergence_tol = 0.01,
  seed = 1L,
  fit_args = list(device = "cuda", batch_size = 16384L),
  predict_args = list(device = "cuda", batch_size = 32768L),
  resume = TRUE
)

2.2 Optional compact wrapper

For a compact dataset, cellcharter_workflow() composes the same stages. It is shown for completeness, but the staged version above is preferable for the full dataset because it exposes each durable checkpoint. If aggregation exceeds available RAM, add filepath = ... and retain that optional HDF5 file with the SPE.

full_spe <- cellcharter_workflow(
  full_spe,
  group_col = "cell_type",
  candidate_k = 2:20,
  checkpoint_dir = "results/CellCharterR_mouse_spleen_v2/autok",
  representation = "X_trVAE",
  sample_col = "sample",
  condition_col = "condition",
  aggregated = "X_cellcharter",
  domain_col = "cellcharter_domain",
  n_layers = 3L,
  condition_groups = c("BALBc", "MRL"),
  n_perms = 100L,
  seed = 1L
)

3 AutoK stability and K selection

The points are all saved neighboring-K Fowlkes–Mallows comparisons from the seven repeated fits; the line is their mean. K=1 is shown as non-estimable because this criterion requires fitted solutions on both neighboring K values. K=4 is the independently selected global maximum. K=11 is annotated only as the predeclared tutorial-matched sensitivity and lies on the secondary K=10–11 stability shoulder.

knitr::include_graphics(manifest$autok_stability_plot)

Neighboring-K Fowlkes–Mallows stability for the full mouse-spleen analysis. K=4 is the independently selected primary resolution; K=11 is highlighted as the tutorial-matched sensitivity resolution.

4 Independently R-selected AutoK primary analysis

primary_k <- manifest$primary_k
primary_paths <- manifest$artifacts$Primary
primary_map <- readRDS(primary_paths[["map_input"]])
primary_enrichment <- readRDS(primary_paths[["enrichment"]])
primary_nhood <- readRDS(primary_paths[["nhood"]])
primary_mrl_balbc <- readRDS(primary_paths[["differential_mrl_balbc"]])
primary_balbc_mrl <- readRDS(primary_paths[["differential_balbc_mrl"]])

4.1 BALBc-1 and early MRL-4 domains

primary_spe <- map_to_spe(primary_map, primary_k)
ggspavis::plotCoords(
  primary_spe,
  annotate = "domain",
  sample_id = "sample_id",
  in_tissue = NULL,
  point_size = 0.1,
  pal = grDevices::hcl.colors(primary_k, "Dynamic")
) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    colour = "Domain",
    title = paste0("Primary R-selected spatial domains: K = ", primary_k)
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 16)

Primary K=4 spatial domains in the BALBc-1 and early MRL-4 slides. 

knitr::kable(
  as.data.frame(table(sample = primary_map$sample, domain = primary_map$domain)),
  caption = "Accessible cell counts underlying the primary domain maps"
)

4.2 Cluster ~ full cell type dot plot (log2 observed/expected)

graphics::par(mar = c(18, 6, 3, 1))
CellCharterR::cellcharter_plot_enrichment(
  primary_enrichment,
  title = paste0("Cluster ~ full cell type enrichment (K=", primary_k, ")")
)

Positive cell-type enrichment in the primary K=4 domains. Darker and larger red points indicate stronger positive log2 fold change. 

primary_enrichment_table <- as.data.frame(
  as.table(primary_enrichment$enrichment), stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
names(primary_enrichment_table) <- c("cell_type", "domain", "log2_enrichment")
knitr::kable(primary_enrichment_table,
             caption = "Values underlying the primary enrichment dot plot")

4.3 BALBc and MRL neighborhood enrichment

graphics::par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(5, 5, 3, 1))
plot_heatmap(
  primary_nhood$BALBc$enrichment, "Healthy spleen — BALBc",
  limits = c(-1, 1), annotate = TRUE
)
plot_heatmap(
  primary_nhood$MRL$enrichment, "Systemic lupus — MRL",
  limits = c(-1, 1), annotate = TRUE
)

Directed observed-minus-expected neighborhood enrichment for BALBc and MRL at the primary K=4 resolution. 

primary_nhood_table <- rbind(
  matrix_long(primary_nhood$BALBc$enrichment, "enrichment", "BALBc"),
  matrix_long(primary_nhood$MRL$enrichment, "enrichment", "MRL")
)
knitr::kable(primary_nhood_table,
             caption = "Values underlying the primary neighborhood heatmaps")

4.4 Differential neighborhood enrichment in both display directions

Both panels reuse one sample-level permutation result (n_perms=100). A star marks directional empirical p <= 0.05; reversing the display negates only the effect and reuses the same permutation counts and p-values.

graphics::par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(5, 5, 3, 1))
plot_heatmap(
  primary_mrl_balbc$effect, "MRL vs BALBc", annotate = TRUE,
  pvalue = primary_mrl_balbc$pvalue, significance = 0.05
)
plot_heatmap(
  primary_balbc_mrl$effect, "BALBc vs MRL", annotate = TRUE,
  pvalue = primary_balbc_mrl$pvalue, significance = 0.05
)

Primary K=4 differential directed neighborhood enrichment in both MRL-minus-BALBc and BALBc-minus-MRL display directions. 

primary_diff_table <- matrix_long(primary_mrl_balbc$effect, "MRL_minus_BALBc")
primary_diff_table$empirical_pvalue <- as.vector(primary_mrl_balbc$pvalue)
knitr::kable(primary_diff_table,
             caption = "Values underlying the primary differential heatmaps")

6 Interpretation boundary

The R-selected AutoK K remains the only primary result. K=11 is a separately fitted tutorial sensitivity analysis. The published H5AD labels remain a separate reference artifact. Representation-learning equivalence is not claimed because the supplied trVAE representation is treated as immutable input. Spatial panels use ggspavis::plotCoords() on SpatialExperiment objects with the exact saved coordinates and labels. Pixel-level equivalence to Squidpy’s plotting stack is not claimed.
